title: Obinutuzumab in Adults With Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease
official: A Phase 2, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Efficacy and Safety Study of Obinutuzumab in Participants With Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease
summary:
The OCTILIA study will evaluate whether adding obinutuzumab to mycophenolate mofetil can improve lung function in people with interstitial lung disease associated with connective tissue diseases.

Approximately 120 participants at 15 sites will be randomly assigned to receive obinutuzumab or a placebo (inactive treatment) while continuing mycophenolate mofetil. Over 24 weeks, researchers will assess lung function, disease worsening, and treatment safety.
conditions: Connective Tissue Disease-associated Interstitial Lung Disease
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age 18 to 79 years, inclusive.
2. Diagnosis of ILD supported by clinically indicated HRCT (within 3 months from randomization), and when available surgical lung biopsy, prior to Screening, and
3. A diagnosis of CTD, based on internationally accepted criteria, including but not limited to one of the following categories:

   * Systemic sclerosis.
   * Inflammatory myopathy (including antisynthetase, anti-MDA5 and overlap syndromes).
   * Mixed CTD.
   * Rheumatoid arthritis.
   * Sjogren's disease.
   * Systemic lupus erythematosus.
   * Undifferentiated CTD.
4. Chest HRCT performed within 3 months of randomization.

   \- Presence of GGO and/or organizing pneumonia CT pattern with or without reticulation or traction bronchiectasis defined by HRCT scan at Screening, with evidence of at least 5% lung involvement and \<40% parenchymal fibrosis, within the whole lung, as determined by the HRCT central reader.
5. Screening (Visit 1) pre-bronchodilator spirometry and DLCO meets ATS quality criteria as determined by either a site Investigator or the central reviewer.
6. Percent predicted FVC ≥ 50% at Screening.
7. Percent predicted DLCO ≥ 40% at Screening, or 30-39% if no significant pulmonary hypertension in the opinion of the investigator
8. FEV1/FVC ratio ≥ 0.70.
9. Background therapy:

   * MMF ≥2g daily, at a stable and clinically tolerated dose for ≥2 weeks before randomization, with no planned dose escalation at randomization
   * Prednisone or equivalent ≤15 mg/day. Could be continued during the trial without dose escalation.
10. No features supporting an alternative diagnosis on transbronchial biopsy, or surgical lung biopsy, if performed prior to Screening.
11. Able to understand and sign written informed consent.
12. For women of childbearing potential: agreement to remain abstinent (refrain from heterosexual intercourse) or use two adequate methods of contraception, including at least one method with a failure rate of \<1% per year, during the 24-week treatment period. A woman is considered to be of childbearing potential if she is postmenarcheal, has not reached a postmenopausal state (≥ 12 continuous months of amenorrhea with no identified cause other than menopause), and has not undergone surgical sterilization (removal of ovaries and/or uterus).

    * Examples of contraceptive methods with a failure rate of \<1% per year include bilateral tubal ligation, male sterilization, established and proper use of hormonal contraceptives that inhibit ovulation, hormone-releasing intrauterine devices, and copper intrauterine devices.
    * The reliability of sexual abstinence should be evaluated in relation to the duration of the clinical trial and the preferred and usual lifestyle of the participant. Periodic abstinence (e.g., calendar, ovulation, symptothermal, or postovulation methods) and withdrawal are not acceptable methods of contraception.
13. For men who are not surgically sterile: agreement to remain abstinent (refrain from heterosexual intercourse) or use contraceptive measures, and agreement to refrain from donating sperm, as defined below:

    * With female partners of childbearing potential, men must remain abstinent or use a condom plus an additional contraceptive method that together result in a failure rate of \<1% per year during the treatment period and for at least 180 days after the last dose of study drug.
    * Men must refrain from donating sperm during this same period.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Emphysema \>40% on HRCT assessed by central reader, or the extent of emphysema is greater than the extent of interstitial lung disease.
2. HRCT scan \> 3 months from randomization.
3. Coexistent clinically significant COPD/emphysema/chronic bronchitis or asthma, which in the opinion of the site principal investigator is the primary driver of symptoms.
4. Pre-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC \< 0.7 at Screening.
5. Cigarette or marijuana smoking or vaping within 3 months of Screening or unwilling to avoid tobacco products, marijuana smoking or vaping throughout the study.
6. Radiation or drug induced ILD, eosinophilic ILD, pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, pulmonary amyloidosis, lymphangioleiomyomatosis, pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis, pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis, smoking-related ILD, obliterative bronchiolitis, IPF.
7. Participants with immunodeficiency syndromes (including hypogammaglobulinemia, i.e., IgG \<400 mg/dl).
8. Suspected or proven untreated tuberculosis.
9. Active systemic infection, positive viral hepatitis, HIV, Covid-19.
10. A history of known Hepatitis B infection with and without antiviral treatment history.
11. Unexplained neurological symptoms suggestive of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy.
12. Pregnant or breast-feeding women, or women of child-bearing potential, not using a reliable contraceptive method.
13. Medications:

    * Receiving nintedanib or pirfenidone or nerandomilast or treprostinil. Initiation of antifibrotic therapy (nintedanib, pirfenidone, or nerandomilast) is prohibited before week 12, then permitted only as protocol-defined rescue for centrally-confirmed ILD progression.
    * Receiving cytotoxic, immunosuppressive, cytokine modulating, or receptor antagonist agents (including but not limited to methotrexate, azathioprine, cyclophosphamide, tocilizumab cyclosporine, or other steroid sparing agent) within 4 weeks of screening (except mycophenolate mofetil).
    * Treatment with anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody within 6 months from visit 1.
    * Receiving systemic corticosteroids equivalent to prednisone \> 15 mg/day or equivalent within 4 weeks before visit 1. Glucocorticoid escalation above baseline (prednisone-equivalent \>15 mg/day), including IV pulse/induction, is prohibited during the double-blind period except as protocol-defined rescue for centrally-confirmed ILD progression or acute exacerbation.
    * Other investigational therapy (participation in research trial) received within 4 weeks of visit 1.
14. On a lung transplant list or plans to undergo lung transplant during the study.
15. Severe heart failure or severe, uncontrolled cardiac disease or other organ co-morbidity that, in the opinion of the Investigator, would preclude the participant's participation in the study.
16. The investigator judges that the participant will be unable to fully participate in the study and complete it for any reason, including inability to comply with study procedures and treatment, or any other relevant medical or psychiatric conditions.
17. Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C).
18. Planning to receive live virus vaccine during therapy.
19. Vaccination with a live vaccine a minimum of 28 days prior to randomization.
20. Severe renal impairment as defined by estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR) \<30 mL/min or the need for dialysis or renal transplant.
21. Absolute Neutrophil Count (ANC) \< 1.5 x 109/L.
22. Platelet count \< 75 x 109/L.
23. Lymphocyte count \>25x 109/L.
24. History of severe allergic or anaphylactic reactions to humanized or murine monoclonal antibodies. Known sensitivity or allergy to murine products.
25. Unable to provide informed written consent.
